paragraphs: SITE Centers Corp., an Ohio corporation (the "Company" or "SITE Centers"), is a self-administered and self-managed Real Estate Investment Trust ("REIT") engaged in the business of owning, leasing, redeveloping and managing shopping centers. Unless otherwise provided, references herein to the Company or SITE Centers include SITE Centers Corp. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries and consolidated and unconsolidated joint ventures.

On October 1, 2024, the Company completed the spin-off of 79 convenience retail properties consisting of approximately 2.7 million square feet of gross leasable area ("GLA") into a separate publicly traded company named Curbline Properties Corp. ("Curbline" or "Curbline Properties"). In connection with the spin-off, on October 1, 2024, the Company, Curbline and Curbline Properties LP (the "Operating Partnership") entered into a Separation and Distribution Agreement (the "Separation and Distribution Agreement"), pursuant to which, among other things, the Company transferred its portfolio of convenience retail properties, $800.0 million of unrestricted cash and certain other assets, liabilities and obligations to Curbline and effectuated a pro rata special distribution of all of the outstanding shares of Curbline common stock to common shareholders of the Company as of September 23, 2024, the record date. On the spin-off date, holders of the Company's common shares received two shares of common stock of Curbline for every one common share of the Company held on the record date.

The spin-off of the convenience properties represented a strategic shift in the Company's business and, as such, the Curbline properties were considered as held for sale as of October 1, 2024 and are reflected as discontinued operations for all periods prior to the spin-off date. Except as otherwise noted, operating statistics cited in this Annual Report on Form 10-K for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 have been adjusted for discontinued operations and properties sold during the year ended December 31, 2024.

The Company is self-administered and self-managed, and therefore, has not engaged, nor does it expect to retain, any REIT advisor. The Company manages all of its shopping centers which are collectively referred to herein as the "Portfolio Properties". At December 31, 2025, the Company owned 19 shopping centers (including 11 shopping centers owned through two unconsolidated joint ventures) totaling 5.0 million square feet of GLA through all its properties (wholly-owned and joint venture). At December 31, 2025, the aggregate occupancy of the Company's operating shopping center portfolio was 85.9% on a pro rata basis, and the average annualized base rent per occupied square foot was $22.61 on a pro rata basis. In addition, the Company owns two adjacent office buildings located in Beachwood, Ohio, totaling approximately 339,000 square feet, yielding approximately 227,000 square feet of GLA, of which the Company occupies approximately 60,000 square feet of GLA and approximately 167,000 square feet of GLA is leased or available to be leased to third parties.
In January, 2026, the Company sold its interest in the RVIP IIIB joint venture (Deer Park Town Center in Deer Park, Illinois).

The primary source of the Company's net income is generated from the rental of the Company's Portfolio Properties to tenants. In addition, the Company generates revenue from its management contracts with its unconsolidated joint ventures and the Shared Services Agreement (defined below) with Curbline.

The Company intends to pursue the marketing and sale of its remaining wholly-owned properties and to monetize the value of its investment in the Dividend Trust Portfolio ("DTP") joint venture. The timing of asset sales may be impacted by general economic conditions, local conditions in the markets in which our remaining properties are situated and other property-specific considerations. The Company's ability and timing to monetize the value of its investment in the DTP joint venture may be impacted by the degree of cooperation of the joint venture partner and the limited rights afforded the Company under the joint venture agreement (including the requirement that the Company obtain the joint venture partner's consent to the sale of individual joint venture properties and distribution of resulting proceeds). As of December 31, 2025, the Company maintained an elevated cash balance pending resolution of the DTP joint venture in order to maximize the Company's alternatives for monetizing its joint venture investment, including through the possible exercise of the joint venture's buy/sell provision.

The Company expects to use proceeds from additional asset sales to pay operating expenses, manage overall liquidity levels, make distributions to shareholders and establish a reserve fund to satisfy projected expenses and known and unknown claims that might arise during the anticipated wind-up of its business. The Company expects to incur significant expenses in connection with the eventual wind-up of its business, including but not limited to the fee applicable to any early termination of the Shared Services Agreement, employee severance costs, discretionary bonuses upon completion of the sales process, costs to terminate office leases,

licenses and other operating contracts, professional fees (including fees of accountants and law firms), costs to comply with ongoing reporting requirements of the Securities Exchange Act 1934 (the "Exchange Act") (until such time as the Company qualifies for relief therefrom), insurance premiums and potential deductibles (including with respect to a "tail" insurance policy for directors and officers), vendor expenses, costs to resolve and streamline the Company's subsidiaries and corporate structure and any claims arising under sale agreements for completed dispositions. For more information regarding risks relating to the Company's disposition and wind-up strategy, see Item 1A. Risk Factors in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

The Company is currently in various stages of marketing several wholly-owned assets for sale, though no assurances can be given that such efforts will result in additional asset sales. As of February 26, 2026, the Company had entered into agreements to sell two properties for which the buyers' general due diligence periods had expired. These transactions are expected to close in the first quarter of 2026. In each case, closing remains subject to customary conditions, including, but not limited to, delivery of estoppel letters from tenants, the accuracy of the Company's representations in all material respects and the absence of material casualty or condemnation events.

The Company expects that rental income and net income will continue to decrease in future periods as compared to corresponding prior year periods as a result of significant disposition activity and declining property revenues. However, the Company's general and administrative expenses will remain elevated prior to the termination of the Shared Services Agreement as a result of the contractual obligations and services owing to Curbline thereunder.

The Company's portfolio as of December 31, 2025, consisted of 19 shopping centers (including 11 centers owned through two unconsolidated joint ventures) located in 13 states. paragraphs: The following is a summary of material risks that could affect the Company's business, results of operations, financial condition, liquidity and cash flows. The risks summarized below are discussed in greater detail in the risk factors that follow and are not the only risks the Company faces. The Company's business operations could also be affected by additional factors that are not presently known to it or that the Company currently considers to be immaterial to its operations. Investors should carefully consider each of the following risks and all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. If any of the following risks actually occur, the Company's business, financial condition or results of operations could be negatively affected.
• The Company may have difficulty selling its remaining real estate investments at attractive prices or at all.
• The Company may have difficulty realizing value from its interest in the DTP joint venture.
• Pursuing the Company's strategy may cause the Company to be subject to U.S. federal income tax.
• The Company expects to pay significant costs in connection with the wind-up of its business.
• The Company expects to establish a reserve fund with proceeds from asset sales in order to satisfy expenses and claims.

paragraphs: The Company is a self-administered and self-managed Real Estate Investment Trust ("REIT") in the business of owning, leasing, redeveloping and managing shopping centers. As of December 31, 2025, the Company's portfolio consisted of 19 shopping centers (including 11 shopping centers owned through two unconsolidated joint ventures). At December 31, 2025, the Company owned 5.0 million square feet of gross leasable area ("GLA") through all its properties (wholly-owned and joint venture). At December 31, 2025, the aggregate occupancy of the Company's operating shopping center portfolio was 85.9% on a pro rata basis, and the average annualized base rent per occupied square foot was $22.61 on a pro rata basis. In addition, at December 31, 2025, the Company owns two adjacent office buildings located in Beachwood, Ohio, totaling approximately 339,000 square feet, yielding approximately 227,000 square feet of GLA, of which the Company occupies approximately 60,000 square feet of GLA and approximately 167,000 square feet of GLA is leased or available to be leased to third parties. In January 2026, the Company sold its interest in the RVIP IIIB joint venture (Deer Park Town Center in Deer Park, Illinois).

In October 2023, the Company announced a plan to spin off a portfolio of convenience retail assets into a separate, publicly traded company to be named Curbline Properties Corp. ("Curbline" or "Curbline Properties") in recognition of the distinct characteristics and opportunities within the Company's unanchored and grocery, lifestyle and power center portfolios. Convenience

properties are generally positioned on the curbline of well-trafficked intersections and major vehicular corridors, offering enhanced access and visibility along with dedicated parking and often include drive-thru units. Convenience properties generally consist of a homogeneous row of primarily small-shop units leased to a diversified mixture of national and local service and restaurant tenants that cater to daily convenience trips from the growing suburban population.

As of September 30, 2024, the Curbline portfolio consisted of 79 wholly-owned convenience retail assets consisting of approximately 2.7 million square feet of GLA. The separation of Curbline was completed on October 1, 2024.

On October 1, 2024, the Company, Curbline and Curbline Properties LP (the "Operating Partnership") entered into a Separation and Distribution Agreement (the "Separation and Distribution Agreement"), which provided for the principal transactions necessary to complete the spin-off, including the allocation among the Company, Curbline and the Operating Partnership of the Company's assets, liabilities and obligations attributable to periods both prior to and following the spin-off. In particular, the Separation and Distribution Agreement provided, among other things, that certain assets relating to Curbline's business were to be transferred to the Operating Partnership or the applicable Curbline subsidiary, including equity interests of certain Company subsidiaries that held assets and liabilities related to Curbline, interests in real property, certain tangible personal property, cash and cash equivalents held in Curbline accounts (including the transfer to Curbline of unrestricted cash of $800.0 million upon consummation of the spin-off) and other assets primarily used or held primarily for use in Curbline's business. The Separation and Distribution Agreement also provided that certain liabilities relating to Curbline's business were to be transferred to the Operating Partnership or the applicable Curbline subsidiary, including liabilities relating to or arising out of the operation of Curbline's business after the effective time of the spin-off and liabilities expressly allocated to Curbline or one of its subsidiaries by the Separation and Distribution Agreement or certain other agreements entered into in connection with the spin-off.

Additionally, the Separation and Distribution Agreement contains provisions that obligate the Company to complete certain redevelopment projects at properties that are owned by Curbline. As of December 31, 2025, these redevelopment projects were estimated to cost $21.3 million to complete.

On October 1, 2024, the Company, Curbline and the Operating Partnership also entered into a Shared Services Agreement (the "Shared Services Agreement"), which provides that, subject to the supervision of the Company's Board of Directors and executives, the Operating Partnership or its affiliates will provide the Company (i) leadership and management services that are of a nature customarily performed by leadership and management overseeing the business and operation of a REIT similarly situated to the Company, including supervising various business functions of the Company necessary for the day-to-day management operations of the Company and its affiliates and (ii) transaction services that are of a nature customarily performed by a dedicated transactions team within an organization similarly situated to the Company, including the provision of personnel at both the leadership and operational levels necessary to ensure effective and efficient preparation, negotiation, execution and implementation of real estate transactions, as well as overseeing post-transaction activities and alignment with the Company's strategic objectives. The Operating Partnership or its affiliates provides the Company with a Chief Executive Officer and Chief Investment Officer but the Company employs its own Chief Financial Officer, Chief Accounting Officer and General Counsel.

The Shared Services Agreement also requires the Company to provide the Operating Partnership and its affiliates the services of its employees and the use or benefit of such other of the Company's assets and resources as may be necessary or useful to establish and operate various business functions of the Operating Partnership and its affiliates in a manner as would be established and operated for a REIT similarly situated to Curbline. The Operating Partnership has the authority to supervise the employees of the Company and its affiliates and direct and control the day-to-day activities of such employees while such employees are providing services to the Operating Partnership or its affiliates under the Shared Services Agreement.

The Operating Partnership pays the Company a fee in the aggregate amount of 2.0% of Curbline's Gross Revenue (as defined in the Shared Services Agreement) during the term of the Shared Services Agreement to be paid in monthly installments each month in arrears no later than the tenth calendar day of each month based upon Curbline's Gross Revenue for the prior month. There is no separate fee paid by the Company in connection with the provision of services by the Operating Partnership or its affiliates under the Shared Services Agreement. Unless terminated earlier, the term of the Shared Services Agreement will expire on October 1, 2027. In the event of certain early terminations of the Shared Services Agreement, the Company will be obligated to pay a termination fee to the Operating Partnership equal to $2.5 million multiplied by the number of whole or partial fiscal quarters remaining in the Shared Services Agreement's three-year term (or $12.0 million in the event the Company terminates the agreement for convenience on October 1, 2026).

The Company is also obligated to provide Curbline Properties and its affiliates with space at the Company's offices located in Beachwood, Ohio, New York, New York and Boca Raton, Florida at no additional cost until October 1, 2027 or such earlier date as the Shared Services Agreement is terminated as a result of a change in control of Curbline Properties or a material breach by Curbline Properties and its affiliates under the Shared Services Agreement (a "Sanctioned Termination Event"). Curbline Properties and its affiliates also have an option exercisable on or prior to October 1, 2027 (or such earlier date as the Shared Services Agreement is

terminated pursuant to a Sanctioned Termination Event) to enter into a lease agreement for office space at the Company's corporate headquarters location in Beachwood, Ohio for an initial five-year term at annual base rent of $8.00 per square foot with the right to extend the lease for up to four successive terms of five years each (with 10% increases in annual base rent for each extension).

The Company, Curbline and the Operating Partnership also entered into a tax matters agreement (the "Tax Matters Agreement"), which governs the rights, responsibilities and obligations of the parties following the spin-off with respect to various tax matters and provides for the allocation of tax-related assets, liabilities and obligations. In addition, the Company, Curbline and the Operating Partnership entered into an employee matters agreement ("the Employee Matters Agreement"), which governs the respective rights, responsibilities, and obligations of the parties following the spin-off with respect to transitioning employees, equity plans and retirement plans, health and welfare benefits, and other employment, compensation, and benefit-related matters.

The Company intends to pursue the marketing and sale of its remaining wholly-owned properties and to monetize the value of its investment in the DTP joint venture. The timing of asset sales may be impacted by general economic conditions, local conditions in the markets in which our remaining properties are situated and other property-specific considerations. The Company's ability and timing to monetize the value of its investment in the DTP joint venture may be impacted by the degree of cooperation of the joint venture partner and the limited rights afforded the Company under the joint venture agreement (including the requirement that the Company obtain the joint venture partner's consent to the sale of individual joint venture properties and distribution of resulting proceeds). See Item 1A. Risk Factors under the captions "Risks Relating to the Company's Strategy–The Company May Have Difficulty Selling Its Remaining Real Estate Investments at Attractive Prices or at All" and "–The Company May Have Difficulty Realizing Value from Its Interest in the DTP Joint Venture."

The Company expects to use proceeds from additional asset sales to pay operating expenses, manage overall liquidity levels, make distributions to shareholders and establish a reserve fund to satisfy projected expenses and known and unknown claims that might arise during the anticipated wind-up of its business. The Company expects to incur significant expenses in connection with the eventual wind-up of its business, including but not limited to the fee applicable to any early termination of the Shared Services Agreement, employee severance costs, discretionary bonuses upon completion of the sales process, costs to terminate office leases, licenses and other operating contracts, professional fees (including fees of accountants and law firms), costs to comply with ongoing reporting requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the "Exchange Act") (until such time as the Company qualifies for relief therefrom), insurance premiums and potential deductibles (including with respect to a "tail" insurance policy for directors and officers), vendor expenses, costs to resolve and streamline the Company's subsidiaries and corporate structure and any claims arising under sale agreements for completed dispositions.

paragraphs: SITE Centers Corp., 一間Ohio公司 (the "Company" or "SITE Centers"), 為一間自營且自管的不動產投資信託 ("REIT")，從事擁有、出租、重新開發及管理購物中心之業務。除非另有說明，本文中提及的Company或SITE Centers包含SITE Centers Corp.及其全資子公司與合併及未合併之合資企業。

於2024年10月1日，Company完成了將約2.7百萬平方英呎的總出租面積 ("GLA") 的79間便利零售商店資產分拆為一間獨立上市的公司，名為Curbline Properties Corp. ("Curbline" or "Curbline Properties")。配合此次分拆，於2024年10月1日，Company、Curbline及Curbline Properties LP (the "Operating Partnership") 簽訂分拆與發行協議 (the "Separation and Distribution Agreement")，根據該協議，Company將其便利零售商店資產組合、800.0百萬美元無限制現金及某些其他資產、負債與義務轉讓給Curbline，並對2024年9月23日為記錄日的Company普通股股東，進行比例發放所有Curbline普通股股份。於分拆日，持有Company普通股股東每持有一股Company普通股，可獲發兩股Curbline普通股。
便利零售商店資產的分拆代表Company業務的重大轉變，因此，Curbline資產自2024年10月1日起被視為待售資產，並於分拆前所有期間列為已終止營運。除非另有說明，本年度報表10-K中2024年及2023年財務資料已調整為已終止營運及2024年財務年度內出售之資產。

Company為自營且自管，因此，未聘請也未預計會聘請REIT顧問。Company管理其所有購物中心，並統稱為 "Portfolio Properties"。於2025年12月31日，Company擁有19間購物中心 (包括透過兩間未合併合資企業所擁有之11間購物中心)，總計5.0百萬平方英呎GLA (包含全資及合資企業之所有資產)。於2025年12月31日，Company營運購物中心組合之總出租率為85.9% (按比例計算)，每平方英呎年化基本租金為22.61美元 (按比例計算)。此外，Company擁有兩棟位於Ohio Beachwood的相鄰辦公大樓，總計約339,000平方英呎，產生約227,000平方英呎GLA，其中Company約佔60,000平方英呎GLA，約167,000平方英呎GLA出租或可供出租予第三方。
於2026年1月，Company出售其在RVIP IIIB合資企業 (Illinois Deer Park Town Center) 的權益。
Company淨收入的主要來源為出租Portfolio Properties予租戶。此外，Company亦透過與未合併合資企業之管理合約及與Curbline之共享服務協議 (定義如下) 產生收入。

Company預計將行銷並出售其餘全資擁有之資產，並實現其在Dividend Trust Portfolio ("DTP") 合資企業之投資價值。資產出售時間可能受總體經濟狀況、本公司剩餘資產所在市場之地方條件及其他資產特定因素影響。Company實現其在DTP合資企業投資價值之能力與時間，可能受合資企業夥伴之合作程度及合資協議中賦予Company之有限權利影響 (包括需取得合資企業夥伴同意出售個別合資企業資產及分配所得款項之要求)。於2025年12月31日，Company維持高額現金以待解決DTP合資企業事宜，以最大化Company實現合資企業投資之選擇，包括可能行使合資企業之買賣條款。
Company預計將使用額外資產出售所得資金用於支付營運費用、管理整體流動性水準、向股東發放紅利，並建立備用基金以應付預期營運終結期間之費用及已知與未知之聲請。Company預計在業務終結時將產生重大費用，包括但不限於任何提前終止共享服務協議之費用、員工離職補償費用、銷售過程完成後之酌情獎金，以及終止辦公租賃之費用,

授權及其它營運契約、專業費用（包括會計師及律師事務所費用）、符合證券交易法 1934 年（"證券交易法"）持續申報要求的費用（直到本公司符合相關豁免條件為止）、保險 premiums 及潛在免賠額（包括與董事及高階管理人員 "尾款" 保險契約相關的部分）、供應商費用、解決並簡化本公司子公司及公司結構的費用，以及因已完成處分契約而產生的任何聲請。有關本公司處分及收攏策略相關風險的更多資訊，請參閱本年度 10-K 報告第 1A 項風險因素。
本公司目前正處於行銷數個全資資產以進行出售的不同階段，但無法保證這些努力會導致額外的資產出售。截至 2026 年 2 月 26 日，本公司已與兩處不動產買方簽訂出售契約，買方的初步審查期已過。這些交易預計於 2026 年第一季完成。在每種情況下，交易完成仍需符合慣例條件，包括但不限於租賃人交付估價書、本公司在所有重大事項上之陳述準確性，以及未發生重大損壞或徵收事件。
本公司預期未來期間的租金收入及淨收入將持續低於相應的前一年期間，這是因為重大處分活動及不動產收入下降所致。然而，本公司一般及行政費用在 Shared Services Agreement 終止前將保持高水準，這是因為與 Curbline 之間的契約義務及服務費用所致。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司資產組合包含 19 個購物中心（包括 11 個透過兩個未合併合資企業所擁有之購物中心），位於 13 個州。以下表格呈現影響基礎租金收入的營運統計資料，按以下資產組合分類總結：按比例合併購物中心資產組合、全資擁有購物中心資產組合及合資企業購物中心資產組合：

paragraphs: 本公司為自行管理及自行經營之不動產投資信託（"REIT"），業務為擁有、出租、重建及管理購物中心。截至2025年12月31日，本公司之資產組合包含19個購物中心（含透過兩個未合併合資企業所擁有之11個購物中心）。截至2025年12月31日，本公司透過所有資產（ wholly-owned 及合資企業）擁有5.0百萬平方英呎之總可出租面積（"GLA"）。截至2025年12月31日，本公司營運購物中心資產組合之總佔用率為85.9%（按比例計算），且每平方英呎平均年化基本租金為22.61美元（按比例計算）。此外，截至2025年12月31日，本公司擁有位於Ohio州Beachwood之兩棟相鄰辦公大樓，總計約339,000平方英呎，產生約227,000平方英呎之GLA，其中本公司佔用約60,000平方英呎之GLA，約167,000平方英呎之GLA已出租或可供出租予第三方。2026年1月，本公司出售其在RVIP IIIB合資企業（位於Illinois州Deer Park之Deer Park Town Center）之權益。
2023年10月，本公司宣佈計畫將一組便利零售資產組合分拆為獨立、公開上市之公司，名為Curbline Properties Corp.（"Curbline" 或 "Curbline Properties"），以反映本公司未設櫃位及超市、生活風格及力量中心資產組合之獨特特徵與機會。便利零售
資產通常位於交通繁忙之路口及主要車道之 curbline，提供增強之通達性與可見度，並包含專用停車空間，常包含 drive-thru 單元。便利零售資產通常為一排同質性之小商店，出租予多元化之國家及地方服務與餐廳租戶，以服務成長中之郊區人口之日常便利需求。
截至2024年9月30日，Curbline 資產組合包含79個 wholly-owned 便利零售資產，總計約2.7百萬平方英呎之GLA。Curbline 之分拆於2024年10月1日完成。

2024年10月1日，本公司、Curbline 及 Curbline Properties LP（"運營合夥企業"）簽訂分拆與發行協議（"分拆與發行協議"），以執行分拆所需之主要交易，包括本公司資產、負債及義務在分拆前後之分配。特別而言，分拆與發行協議規定，與Curbline業務相關之某些資產應轉移至運營合夥企業或適用之Curbline子公司，包括持有與Curbline相關資產及負債之本公司子公司之股權、實體不動產、某些有形動產、Curbline帳戶中持有之現金及現金等價物（包括分拆完成時轉移至Curbline之無限制現金800.0百萬美元）及其他主要用於或持有用於Curbline業務之資產。分拆與發行協議亦規定，與Curbline業務相關之某些負債應轉移至運營合夥企業或適用之Curbline子公司，包括分拆生效後Curbline業務運作所產生之負債，以及分拆與發行協議或分拆相關之其他協議明確分配至Curbline或其子公司之負債。
此外，分拆與發行協議包含條款，義務本公司完成Curbline所擁有之資產之某些重建項目。截至2025年12月31日，這些重建項目預估總成本為21.3百萬美元。

2024年10月1日，本公司、Curbline 及運營合夥企業亦簽訂共用服務協議（"共用服務協議"），規定在本公司董事會及高階主管監督下，運營合夥企業或其附屬公司將為本公司提供（i）領導與管理服務，為類似本公司之REIT常見之領導與管理服務，包括監督本公司各項業務功能，以確保本公司及其附屬公司日常管理運作，以及（ii）交易服務，為類似本公司之組織常見之專門交易團隊所提供之服務，包括提供領導及運營層級之人力，以確保有效且高效之不動產交易準備、談判、執行與落實，以及監督交易後活動與符合本公司戰略目標。運營合夥企業或其附屬公司為本公司提供首席執行長與首席投資長，但本公司聘僱其自身之首席財務長、首席會計長與總法律顧問。
共用服務協議亦規定本公司應為運營合夥企業及其附屬公司提供員工服務及使用或受益於本公司之其他資產與資源，以建立及運作運營合夥企業及其附屬公司之各項業務功能，如同為類似Curbline之REIT所建立及運作。運營合夥企業有權監督本公司及其附屬公司之員工，並指揮及控制其在根據共用服務協議為運營合夥企業或其附屬公司提供服務期間之日常活動。

營運合夥人會向本公司支付費用，總計為 Curbline 毛利率收入（依共用服務協議所定義）的 2.0%，於共用服務協議期間內，每月以現金方式支付，於每個月的第十個營業日之前支付，基於 Curbline 前一個月的毛利率收入。本公司不會因營運合夥人或其關係企業根據共用服務協議提供服務而支付任何額外費用。除非提前終止，共用服務協議的期限將於 2027 年 10 月 1 日屆滿。若因某些提前終止情況而終止共用服務協議，本公司將需向營運合夥人支付終止費用，金額為 2.5 百萬美元乘以共用服務協議三年期限中剩餘的完整或部分財務季度數（若本公司於 2026 年 10 月 1 日因便利而終止協議，則為 12.0 百萬美元）。

本公司亦有義務為 Curbline Properties 及其關係企業提供空間，於本公司位於俄亥俄州 Beachwood、紐約州紐約及佛羅裏達州 Boca Raton 的辦公室內，不收取額外費用，直至 2027 年 10 月 1 日或共用服務協議因 Curbline Properties 或其關係企業因控制權變更或重大違約而終止為止（稱為「制裁終止事件」）。Curbline Properties 及其關係企業亦有權於 2027 年 10 月 1 日或共用服務協議因制裁終止事件而終止時，簽訂租賃協議，租賃本公司位於俄亥俄州 Beachwood 的總部辦公室空間，租賃期限為初始五年，年租金為每平方英尺 8.00 美元，並有權於每個五年期續約四次，每次租金增加 10%。
終止係根據受制裁終止事件而進行，以簽訂租賃契約，租賃本公司總部所在地Ohio州Beachwood的辦公室空間，初始租賃期限為五年，年基礎租金為每平方英尺8.00美元，並有權將租賃契約延長至最多四個連續的五年期（每個延長期的年基礎租金增加10%）。

本公司預計將積極行銷並出售其餘所有自有不動產，並實現其在 DTP 聯營公司的投資價值。資產出售的時間可能受到總體經濟狀況、本公司剩餘不動產所在市場的當地條件及其他不動產特定因素的影響。本公司實現其在 DTP 聯營公司投資價值的能力與時間，可能受到聯營公司合作程度及聯營協議中賦予本公司有限權利的影響（包括本公司需取得聯營公司同意才能出售個別聯營不動產及分配所得金額的規定）。請參閱第 1A 項「風險因素」標題為「本公司可能難以以有吸引力的價格或完全出售其餘不動產投資」及「本公司可能難以實現其在 DTP 聯營公司的投資價值」的內容。

本公司預計將利用額外資產出售所得資金，用以支付營運費用、管理整體流動性水平、向股東發放分紅，並建立一個準備金以應付預期的費用及已知與未知的聲請，這些聲請可能在本公司業務預期收尾期間產生。本公司預計在業務最終收尾期間將產生重大費用，包括但不限於任何提前終止共用服務協議的費用、員工離職補償費用、銷售過程完成時的酌情獎金、終止辦公室租賃、許可證及其他營運契約的費用、專業費用（包括會計師與律師事務所的費用）、符合 1934 年證券交易法（稱為「證券交易法」）持續報告要求的費用（直至本公司符合該法的豁免條件為止）、保險 premiums 及潛在免賠額（包括與董事及高階管理人員「尾款」保險政策相關的部分）、供應商費用、解決並簡化本公司子公司及公司結構的費用，以及任何因已完成處分的銷售協議而產生的聲請。

本公司預計將利用額外資產出售所得資金，用以支付營運費用、管理整體流動性水平、向股東發放分紅，並建立一個準備金以應付預期的費用及已知與未知的聲請，這些聲請可能在本公司業務預期收尾期間產生。本公司預計在業務最終收尾期間將產生重大費用，包括但不限於任何提前終止共用服務協議的費用、員工離職補償費用、銷售過程完成時的酌情獎金、終止辦公室租賃、許可證及其他營運契約的費用、專業費用（包括會計師與律師事務所的費用）、符合 1934 年證券交易法（稱為「證券交易法」）持續報告要求的費用（直至本公司符合該法的豁免條件為止）、保險 premiums 及潛在免賠額（包括與董事及高階管理人員「尾款」保險政策相關的部分）、供應商費用、解決並簡化本公司子公司及公司結構的費用，以及任何因已完成處分的銷售協議而產生的聲請。

paragraphs: 以下為可能影響本公司業務、營運成果、財務狀況、流動性及現金流之重大風險摘要。下列風險內容於後續風險因素部分有更詳細說明，並非本公司所面臨之唯一風險。本公司之業務運作亦可能受其他尚未知悉或本公司目前認為對其運作不具重大影響之因素影響。投資人應謹慎考量下列各項風險，以及本年度10-K表報表中所載之其他資訊。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成負面影響。
• 本公司可能難以以具吸引力之價格或完全出售其餘留之不動產投資。
• 本公司可能難以從其在DTP合資公司之權益中實現價值。
• 追求本公司之策略可能使本公司成為美國聯邦所得稅之納稅義務人。
• 本公司預期會因業務收攏而產生重大費用。
• 本公司預期會以資產出售所得資金設立備用基金，以支付費用及聲請賠償。
